author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

text:
There are many AI chip design EDA startups? Most of them are so secretive.

If they are as good as they claimed, why don't they design some classic chips like 4004 or 8086 in a public GitHub repo, show the world the true power of their tools. Even better, they can record the run on Youtube, so the potential users know exactly what they are getting.

If they are afraid that their secret sauce will get copied away from a YouTube video, are they really building a real product with a real moat?

comments.text: Startup ecosystem has become a joke ... it's now only about fame and money. I have seen that the founders of many of these startups don't even have a background in IC design. It is a joke.

author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

comments.text: I've yet to see any "real reason to believe" from AI EDA startups. Models from Anthropic and OpenAI can to chip design tasks amazingly well, no need for special EDA AI tools. Tools on top of AI for EDA, whether in-house or commercial just seem like bloat that get in the way when a good engineer can get the the models to do what they want

comments.text: I would argue that you can build a product, but I also asked myself the question about the moat. If it all runs with the same LLM in the background, then a lot of the moat will be about usability, stability and how well expert/process knowledge is being guided by it.

author.name: Rahul Bhagwat
author.headline: Designing chips and chip design software

comments.text: openada does something like this for their analog assistant, which is kinda cool https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lKj8TV-Jyy0

Actually that's a good idea. But the 4004 is not a fair example, you suggest it because it is very old so it is simple in theory. In practice processors are an extremely complex chip design problem for agentic flows, because it is not only the rtl but also the sw and perhaps tools on top of that. Some startups showed end to end riscv cores but the entire riscv stack is available online. My point is that sharing Verilog designs as open source to show AI EDA capability is a real good idea but CPU chips are a high bar to start with.
